the development of a software system that allows users with motorical disabilities to communicate with other people using a computer, and to increase their typing rates.

the inclusion of a word prediction system into a switch-based writing system for people with disabilities is a good idea.

the inclusion of word pairs and tripos models improves the prediction performance, and the use of stochastic context free grammar is a good complement to the statistical models, improving the prediction performance in some cases.

the word prediction system described here, based on statistical and grammatical techniques, is a very useful tool for users with motor disabilities, and can be easily integrated into any software for communication, as the system is independent of the application, and it is a stand alone module.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in general, the best results have been obtained using grammatical methods, and in particular, the best results were obtained with the bipos model and the tripos model, with a relative reduction of the typing time of 30% and 35% respectively.

, in the case of the word prediction system integrated in a Spanish aid for people with severe motorical disabilities, we have obtained a typing rate of 8.6 wpm with the grammatical model (SCFG) and 9.2 with the statistical model (trios).

we have developed a word prediction system for the Spanish language, which is integrated in an aid to help users with motorical disabilities to write, and which is also integrated in several software applications for writing, and in a web-based application to write in the Spanish language.

the word prediction system has been integrated in the software for people with disabilities, and that this integration has been very well received by them.
